The original definition of 'representative' (pre-2020) means an employee or agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that adviser.

The 2020 amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' is broader and includes any member, partner, officer, director, employee or sales staff engaged in providing investment advisory services, including client-facing persons, but excludes persons who perform only clerical or administrative functions without client interface.

Therefore, the 2020 definition covers a broader set of persons within an investment advisory firm than the original 'representative' definition; they do not cover exactly the same set of persons.

An agent may not move a payment that is already scheduled to a different date by rescheduling another payment, because the servicing tooling cannot move, amend, or cancel a payment already scheduled.

If a customer requests to move an existing instalment to a different date, the agent must verify the customer and escalate the case to a human rather than attempt an automatic date change.

citations.quote:
## Payments

An agent may schedule a **new** one-off payment against an active loan: due no earlier than today
and no more than **60 days** ahead, for an amount between **₹100** and **₹5,00,000**. A loan that
has been closed takes no further payments.

The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled, and
scheduling a second payment does not replace the first — it creates a second obligation, and the
customer will be collected for both. So a request to *move* an existing instalment to a different
date is not something an agent may do by scheduling another payment. Verify the customer, tell
them plainly that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human. A
request to add a payment the customer does not already owe — a part payment, an extra payment —
is an ordinary scheduling request and needs no escalation.

## Identity before money

No agent may move money, change a payment obligation, or forgive a charge until the customer's
identity has been verified on the current contact. This applies to scheduling a payment, cancelling
an auto-debit mandate, waiving a fee, and applying a hardship plan. It applies even when the
customer is plainly who they say they are, even when they have called before, and even when they
are impatient.

Verification means confirming the last four digits of the registered mobile number against the
account record. A verification that has been recorded on this contact is good for the remainder of
the contact and no longer.

If verification fails, say so plainly, do not hint at the correct answer, and do not offer a second
route to the same outcome. Two failed attempts on one contact end the automated journey: hand the
case to a human. A customer who cannot verify may still be given general information that is not
account-specific, and may still be told how to verify through the app.

Reading a loan record, looking at payment history, requesting a document, sending a statement to
the address already on file, and escalating are not money movements and do not require prior
verification. Sending a statement anywhere other than the address already on the record is not
permitted at all; the contact record must be updated first, through the normal contact-change
route.

The original version of Regulation 16(3) allows withdrawal of a credit rating only if the company whose security is rated is wound up, merged, or amalgamated with another company.

The 2018-amended version of Regulation 16(3) expands the grounds for withdrawal by adding that a rating can also be withdrawn as specified by the Board from time to time, in addition to the earlier conditions of winding up, merger, or amalgamation.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Regulation 16(3) (pre-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company.

Passage B:
Regulation 16(3) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-05-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company, or as may be specified by the Board from time to time.

Before ordering an inspection under the SEBI Investment Advisers Regulations, 2013, SEBI must give the investment adviser not less than ten days advance notice.

SEBI can dispense with the ten days notice and order an inspection without prior notice if it is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given; this must be by an order in writing.

citations.quote: Regulation 24(1): Before ordering an inspection under regulation 23, the Board shall give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection of the affairs of the investment adviser be taken up without such notice.

Regulation 9(e) requires the promoter to maintain this minimum shareholding of 26% for a minimum period of three years from the date of grant of registration by the Board.
